title: Collection Health
description: Is the pipeline itself working? Every threshold alert in this stack is silently disarmed when an agent stops shipping — 'no data' never crosses a threshold. This dashboard is where that becomes visible.

panels.title: Machines silent
panels.description: Seen in the last 24h, sending nothing now.

panels.title: Dropped log entries (15m)
panels.description: Dropped, not buffered — these entries are gone. Usually a Loki rate limit or an entry older than reject_old_samples_max_age.

panels.title: Agent status
panels.description: `Last seen` is derived over a 24h range rather than from the live series, because `up` disappears 5 minutes after an agent stops — the very case this table exists to show. `Lag` is how far behind the agent's write queue is.

panels.title: Samples in vs shipped
panels.description: These two lines should sit on top of each other. A gap means the WAL is absorbing the difference.

panels.title: Write lag
panels.description: Seconds between the newest sample collected and the newest sample acknowledged by the server. Sustained growth ends in data loss when the WAL ages out.

panels.title: Pending samples in WAL
panels.description: Samples read out of the WAL but not yet acknowledged.

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: Approaching the scrape interval means the exporter is too slow and samples will start being missed.

panels.title: Series per target
panels.description: Sudden growth is usually a cardinality explosion — a new label with unbounded values.

panels.title: Prometheus head series
panels.description: Active series in memory. The main driver of the server's RAM use.

panels.title: Server disk free
panels.description: If this reaches zero the entire stack stops — including the alerting that would have told you.

panels.title: Rejected by Prometheus (1h)
panels.description: Most often out-of-order samples during a client's WAL replay. If this is non-zero after an outage, raise storage.tsdb.out_of_order_time_window.

panels.title: Stack component health
panels.description: 1 = responding. Everything else on this page depends on these.

panels.title: Rule evaluation
panels.description: Failing rules produce no series, so whatever they compute is quietly missing from dashboards and alerts.
